input:
what is the android app structure like?
can it control things on the densor like sampling rate or similar?

or is it just retrieval and charging?

output.text: I’ll check the Android app and its device protocol to see what it can configure and how retrieval and charging fit in.

The app has a Densor settings screen that writes the sampling interval, sensor switches, startup delay, and clock selection over NFC. I’m checking how the firmware applies those settings and how the charging and data screens work.

Yes—the Android app can configure the **NFC-harvesting Densor**, including its sampling interval. It handles more than retrieval and charging.

It’s a **Java/XML app adapted from ST’s ST25 NFC application**, with an `app` module and an NFC reader-interface module. The Densor interface is organized into [tabs in `ST25DVActivity`](/mnt/shared/Git/densor/NFC_harvester_battery_free/software/source_ST25NFCApplication_V3_9/app/src/main/java/com/st/st25nfc/type5/st25dv/ST25DVActivity.java:118):

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Densor settings](/mnt/shared/Git/densor/NFC_harvester_battery_free/software/source_ST25NFCApplication_V3_9/app/src/main/java/com/st/st25nfc/densor/DensorSettingsFragment.java:239) | Sets the sampling interval in **seconds or minutes**; enables/disables temperature, photodiode, and accelerometer measurements; sets a **0–59 minute startup delay**; selects the RTC’s internal RC or external crystal clock. |
| [Time/start/charging](/mnt/shared/Git/densor/NFC_harvester_battery_free/software/source_ST25NFCApplication_V3_9/app/src/main/java/com/st/st25nfc/densor/TimeSyncFragment.java:229) | Writes the recording start timestamp, resets or wipes recorded data, provides a wipe-and-start action, and puts Densor into charging mode. |
| [Data view](/mnt/shared/Git/densor/NFC_harvester_battery_free/software/source_ST25NFCApplication_V3_9/app/src/main/java/com/st/st25nfc/densor/DataViewFragment.java:248) | Downloads stored measurements and plots temperature, photodiode readings, acceleration, and supply voltage. |

There are also inherited tag-information, raw-memory, and system-information tabs.

The configuration is implemented end to end: **the app writes settings into NFC tag memory; the microcontroller reads them over I²C**, samples the selected sensors, stores the results, and sleeps for the configured interval. See the [firmware settings and measurement loop](/mnt/shared/Git/densor/NFC_harvester_battery_free/software/DentalSensor_StorageProject/Core/Src/main.c:466).

**“Sampling rate” here means the interval between logged measurements**, such as one measurement every 10 seconds. The UI accepts interval values of 0–59 in seconds or minutes; it doesn’t expose subsecond sampling or accelerometer range controls. Configuration and retrieval require NFC proximity, while recording runs on the device.

This is based on the checked-in app and firmware; I haven’t tested it on hardware.
